proof:
# Every coordinate product of an exponential cap centroid

Let Y_0,...,Y_d be independent unit-rate exponentials, let c be a real
vector, and suppose P=Pr(sum c_i Y_i>=0)>0. Write
nu_i=E(Y_i | sum c_iY_i>=0). Then

    product_(i=0)^d nu_i>=P,
    product_(i!=j) nu_i>=P for every j.             (1)

All conditional means are positive and finite. No hypothesis on the
numbers of positive, negative, or zero coefficients is required. This
concerns the centroid of a CAP, not the centroid of its boundary section.

## Full product

The conditional joint density is exp(-sum y_i)1_C/P on the cone
C={y>=0:sum c_i y_i>=0}. Scaling its integral gives

    integral_C exp(-s sum y_i)dy=s^(-(d+1))P.

Differentiation at one yields sum nu_i=d+1. If q is the independent
product exponential density with means nu_i, direct integration gives

    D_KL(p||q)=log[(product_i nu_i)/P].              (2)

The integral is finite; nonnegativity follows from log u<=u-1 applied
to u=q/p on C. In fact its integral is at most integral_C q-1<=0.
This proves the first assertion. It is strict when c has both signs,
because C then excludes an open part of the orthant to which q gives
positive mass.

## Omission of a positive coefficient

Suppose c_j>0. Integrating Y_j out shows that the conditional density
of z=(Y_i)_(i!=j) is exp(-psi(z))/P on the whole orthant, where

    psi(z)=sum_(i!=j) z_i
       +max{-sum_(i!=j)(c_i/c_j)z_i,0}.

This function is homogeneous of degree one and bounded above and below
by positive multiples of sum z_i. Its scaling identity implies
E psi=d. Comparing with the product exponential density whose means
are the corresponding nu_i gives the exact identity

    D_KL=log[(product_(i!=j)nu_i)/P]>=0.            (3)

This proves the assertion for c_j>0, including cases where the other
coefficients are zero. Equality is permitted when the other nonzero
coefficients all have one sign; if they include both signs, psi has
two different linear gradients on open sets and the inequality is strict.

## Omission of a nonpositive coefficient

If c_j<=0, the conditional probability g(t) of the cap event given
Y_j=t is nonincreasing. For independent copies T,T' of Y_j,

    2 Cov(T,g(T))=E[(T-T')(g(T)-g(T'))]<=0.

Thus E(Y_j 1_C)<=P and nu_j<=1. Dividing the full product inequality
by nu_j proves the second assertion in (1). This also covers c_j=0.

## Ordinary simplex interpretation

If X is uniform in a d-simplex, let H be a halfspace of positive cap
fraction P and let a_i be the barycentric coordinates of its cap
centroid. The exponential representation Y=G X, with independent
G~Gamma(d+1,1), shows nu_i=(d+1)a_i. Therefore

    (d+1)^(d+1) product_i a_i>=P,
    (d+1)^d product_(i!=j)a_i>=P for every j.

The cone event depends only on X, so the independence of G remains
valid after cap conditioning. These are ordinary cap-centroid product
inequalities. Replacing the cap centroid by the boundary-section
centroid would be a different theorem and is not asserted here.
